recipes.name: Roasted Loin of Pork with Pan Gravy
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Make several small slits in top of pork roast; place into a roasting pan.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add garlic, oregano, cayenne, thyme, mustard powder, and black pepper; cook and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute. Remove from the heat.
Spread spice mixture all over pork and rub into slits. Place onion, carrots, and celery around pork; season with salt and pepper.

Roast in the preheated oven for 1 hour 45 minutes. Increase the heat to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and continue cooking until pork is browned and an instant-read meat thermometer inserted into the center of the roast reads at least 150 degrees F (65 degrees C), about 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let stand for 10 minutes. Recheck the temperature; it should be at least 160 degrees F (75 degrees C) before slicing.

While the pork is resting, place the roasting pan with vegetables and pan drippings over a stove burner set to medium heat. Whisk in flour and simmer to remove raw taste, about 3 minutes. Whisk in stock, a little at a time, until gravy is thickened.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Loin of Pork with Pan Gravy
raw_recipe.description: Make an easy pork gravy with pan drippings and stock, then ladle it over slices of deliciously seasoned roasted pork loin for a flavor-packed main dish.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful seasonings! It could be too spicy for some - know your audience - for us this was perfect. I took the roast out of the refrigerator for about an hour to warm up. I used olive oil instead of butter to cook the spices and I ended up using more course ground pepper - what can I say, we love pepper. I cooked the roast at 300 until it reached 125 degrees and then turned the oven up to 425 and cooked to 145. Took out and rested while I did the gravy. I did do the gravy a bit different. I used 2 T butter and 2 T flour - made a roux in a seperate pan. I removed the cooked vegetables and strained the juices from the baking pan - I used the drippings plus 1 cup pork stock to make the gravy. Very good!

This one is a definite keeper! It was delicious. I didn’t have cayenne pepper on hand, so I substituted 1/4 teaspoon of crushed red pepper. I also used vegetable stock instead of pork stock. The recipe doesn’t call for it, but I poured a generous amount of vegetable stock into the roasting pan before it went into the oven. That kept the vegetables from burning up. Then I didn’t bother to strain the vegetables out of the gravy. They were beautifully cooked and too inviting and delicious to waste them. I also sautéed sliced baby bella mushrooms and stirred them into the gravy as a final step. I didn’t measure the vegetable stock. I just kept stirring it in until the gravy reached the consistency I wanted. The pork came out very tender, flavorful, and moist, and the gravy was amazing! I served it with Amish butter noodles, which made the perfect complement. This meal will become a regular part of the rotation at our house!

The flavor was Amazing! Only change I made was to put all spices in frying pan with 1/2 stick of butter and sear the loin on all sides. After placing loin in roasting pan, I pored the pan contents over the loin, then deglazed the pan with a cup of hot water and added this to the bottom of the roasting pan. This helped to make an awesome gravy.

Great little recipe! I had no celery, so I subbed a green apple to make sure there'd be enough moisture. Left out the cayenne, but added celery salt because I wanted the celery flavoring. Went by the recipe, except that I cooked it in my Nesco 6-quart roaster at 300. Sprayed the interior of the roaster with nonstick spray, put the fixin's in while the roaster was cold, turned it on, put the lid on, and once the temperature hit 300 degrees, set my timer for an hour in order to check it. The roast was at 150 when the timer went off, so I let it rest for 10 minutes (temp continued to rise), strained the drippings, added a little chicken bouillon and made gravy using cornstarch. Gravy and meat were outstanding; the roast was melt-in-your-mouth tender. Served with boiled red taters and green beans. Awesome. Thanks for sharing!

Cooked 3 whole pork loins for our Sunday School Class Christmas luncheon. The only thing I changed was to brine the Pork loins in a simple salt/sugar brine overnight. before roasting and I cooked them in roasting bags. Soooo tender and a welcome change from turkey or ham.

It was very tasty. I did a few things differently. First, I cooked it at 375 for 20 mins per pound. It came out perfectly! It very tender and a medium rare to medium. I also, like others, used less cayenne pepper. The roast was pretty lean, so it didn't render a lot of juice for making the gravy. Next time, i might add a little liquid to the pan. I also substituted chicken stock for the pork stock.

You can just about double the spices in the butter mixture. I found this roast a little under seasoned without the gravy. I also threw 3 tbsp of butter into the mirepoix before sifting the flour into it, and you should also double the amount of stock the recipe calls for. I did 3/4 cup of stock and it was barely enough for a ~2 lb roast (granted the gravy was so good we all poured it all over the potatoes and roasted cauliflower that I also made, but still; you do not want to not have enough gravy). A note re other reviews: if you're finding you need to pour broth over the mirepoix before roasting, or that it burns in the oven, you do not have enough of a fat cap on your pork loin or you're using too lean of a roast. I would not use the lean end of a long loin (like the loins you get from Costco) for this recipe. I used the rib end, untrimmed, and there were plenty of drippings.

Hubby wanted a pork roast and so grabbed one from the freezer, not taking into account that it was frozen. So, out comes the Instant Pot pressure cooker and we loves ours.

We followed the recipe exactly, and it came out tender, with a nice flavor that wasn't overpowering. It wasn't as nice looking as the photo but it tasted good. We added potatoes, carrots and onions and I strained the broth, we did add some veggie broth to have enough liquid. Added the flour to a small amount of broth and let it cook on the stove until it thicken. 
The only change we will make the next time we make it and it doesn't have to do with the recipe exactly is let it cook a few minutes longer, one part was a bit tough and we put the potatoes and carrots in too early, they were a bit overcooked, but still very good. 
We will definitely use the recipe again for a roast and he took some over to our neighbor as his wife died recently; we always have left overs so share them.

This recipe sounded like it would be great, so I gave it a try. Way too much spice for me.Seasonings are meant to complement the meat,but even after using half the recommended amount of cayenne all the seasonings overpowered the pork. I would reduce the cayenne to 1/8 teaspoon and reduce the black pepper and oregano to 1/8-1/4tsp. Also add more butter or a couple of tablespoons of EVOO.I also mix the flour into cold water or broth then add to the simmering drippings. I would add 1/4 tsp gravy master and 1T dry minced onion to the gravy and simmer to thicken/reduce and then strain.I like spicey but I also like to taste the flavor of the meat. Thanks :)

This was easy to make, and I got raves about its flavor, especially the gravy. My pork loin was about twice as large as this recipe called for, so I just increased the ingredients accordingly. (Except for the pan gravy -- I used an 8 oz. bottle of apple juice for broth in the roaster, a little more than twice as much butter, and just over the designated amount of flour. It all came out fine!)

I never realized that 1/2 teaspoon of cayenne pepper could crank up soooo much heat in a recipe!! Once we got past that, it had pretty good flavor. I do not have pork stock (never have!), so used chicken bone broth. What I did was mix all the leftovers together including the veggies, gravy and made a casserole out of it. Now, that was surprisingly good!! I served this with baked sweet potatoes and salad. My hubby thought the sweet potatoes complimented the pork. Sort of mellowed the heat! Next time for me, anyway, is to add just a 'dash' of cayenne!
I liked this recipe. It was very good. I only switched the flour for corn starch dissolved in cold water (2 tsp/4 tbsp cold water). The sauce was very good. Will make it again.

I used a 4 lb bone-in loin roast, added about 20 mins to bake time but otherwise followed the recipe as written. The pork was very juicy and tender. I like hot things but, after scoffing at all the reviews complaining about the spice level, I have to agree that I didn't care for it. I guess I don't want spice in my gravy. Next time I'd omit the cayenne. Oh, I like a lot of gravy so ended up tripling the amount of stock used for gravy and I used and immersion blender to blend in the vegetables.
I like the seasonings, but I cut back on the cayenne pepper. I made it in a crockpot. It’s a keeper for me.

I made it and it was tasty and straightforward to do. But, it was quite tough. I followed the recipe exactly but the piece of loin I used was about half the size called for in the recipe. I adjusted the time to cook accordingly. Maybe it was just the piece I used was tough.

I'm making this a second time.....the only changes are less flour and more broth (and I use chicken instead of pork). I do add 1/2 cup of broth to the vegetables before putting the roast in the oven. When doing the gravy, reduce the flour to a tbsp and increase the broth to 1 cup. My general rule is a cup of broth for each tbsp of flour

Easy and flavorful. I like recipes that are easy, don’t take a lot of time or ingredients. Plus the added bonus that the ingredients you need for this recipe are usually the ones you already have on hand. My family loved it. It’s a keeper

Delicious! I used chicken broth instead of pork since that is what I had in hand. I poured a bit of the broth over the veggies while cooking so they would not dry out. I would highly recommend this recipe. It was a hit in my house.
There were no drippings when done, just black gunk. Vegetables were dry. This either needs liquid while cooking or needs to be covered. No gravy today.
Very tender and flavorful recipe. I made as directed and it turned out great! Served with baked potatoes.
